- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a recent spike in sentiment, apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% below forecast, apply a downward bias correction of 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.3), adjust forecast to mean-revert toward 10–15 day moving average of recent prices.  
- Avoid forecasting below 68% of recent 10-day low if sentiment is neutral or negative — this triggers a “floor” correction rule.
